title: Quadratic unshifted resolvent collapse and low-shift exclusion

spectral_consequence.general_low_shift: If a_N<=c_g N^2-r_N with r_N tending to infinity, then inf spec(H_N-a_N)>=r_N and ||(H_N-a_N+lambda)^(-1)||<=1/(r_N+lambda) tends to zero
spectral_consequence.subquadratic_shift: In particular every scalar recentering a_N=o(N^2) leaves the spectral bottom tending to plus infinity and the resolvent collapsing to zero in norm
spectral_consequence.operator_ceiling: Zero is not the resolvent of a densely defined self-adjoint operator, so these low shifts cannot have a finite nontrivial self-adjoint strong-resolvent limit
spectral_consequence.rate_ceiling: The O(N^-2) statement is an upper norm bound from a nonsharp energy lower constant; no matching resolvent asymptotic is claimed
